editorial.headline: KBLI 26410 and the Industrial Side of Screens
editorial.standfirst: Television, monitor, and display manufacturing is nationally open to foreign investment and, on this record, not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 26410 sits in the physical economy behind the screens people usually treat as finished objects. The record defines it as the manufacturing and assembly of televisions, television receivers and combinations, television monitors, and display products such as videotron. In plain English, this is not broadcasting, content, software, installation, or retail. It is the industrial activity of making and assembling the viewing hardware itself: the television set, the monitor, and the larger display format that turns electronics into a visible surface.

That distinction matters because the activity is open across the full business-scale ladder listed in the record: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. A very small assembler and a large industrial operation are therefore both inside the scale universe for this code, as long as the registered activity remains the making and assembling of the products described. The scope is broad enough to cover conventional television units and modern display formats, but still disciplined: the anchor is manufacturing and assembly, not the commercial life that may come before or after the object leaves the factory.

The national investment position is unusually clean. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. For a foreign-owned company reading this record, the national answer is therefore not a partial opening or a negotiated carve-out; the record states that the activity is open and allows full foreign ownership. The source attached to that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. No additional capital threshold, licence name, tax treatment, timetable, or technical permit appears in the slim record, so none should be inferred from the national opening alone.

Bali adds the practical second reading. The province’s moratorium rule is severe in its wording: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. But this particular record is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason stated as: “OSS risk at scale Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi → not blocked by moratorium.” The honest conclusion is therefore straightforward. Nationally, KBLI 26410 is foreign-open up to 100%. On the Bali side, this record does not mark it as closed by the PMA moratorium. The caveat is not a hidden Bali percentage or a local quota; the only Bali-side fact in the record is that its higher-risk reading keeps it outside the moratorium block described here.
editorial.pullQuote: The honest conclusion is therefore straightforward: nationally, KBLI 26410 is foreign-open up to 100%, and this record does not mark it as closed by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
